title: A task that waits for two others
context: How would you run a task only after two other tasks have finished?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Use CompletableFuture. Start the two tasks with supplyAsync, then combine them with `thenCombine` or `allOf(...).thenRun`. The combined task runs when both futures complete, without blocking a thread while it waits. CountDownLatch also works: the dependent task awaits a latch counted down by the two tasks. Latches block a thread, so CompletableFuture is better in a pool with limited threads.

points.title: Non-blocking join
points.why: thenCombine or allOf runs the dependent step when results are ready, without holding a thread.

points.title: CountDownLatch alternative
points.why: A latch works, but its await blocks a thread until the count reaches zero.
